_comment: The environment values this stack owns in the scope's settings.json `env` block (the project's .claude/settings.json, or the account file for a global install). ONE source for the three guided commands: setup asks the `ask: true` rows on its environment screen, configure step 9 shows and changes them, validate reconciles what is on disk against this list - a row absent from the file is a MISSING key the release introduced, a `renamed_from` still present is the old spelling, and a value failing `validate` is flagged with the expected shape. The installers seed every row ABSENT-ONLY on install and update (and apply the renames first, value carried over), so this catalog and the two installer twins must agree - `npm run lint` fails when they drift. Adding a variable: add the row here, seed it in both twins, and, when it replaces an older name, add the rename pair to migrations.json and give every consumer an old-name fallback. A row may carry `group_off`: it and every row naming it in `asked_with` are ONE feature, so the question that asks it also offers switching the feature off, which writes that value to the whole group (the walks never invent an off answer for a row without it). A row may also carry `secret: true`, and any key matching `secret_key_pattern` is treated the same way whether or not it has a row: its VALUE is never printed, never echoed back as a default, and never asked for through the chat - the walks report `set (N chars)` or `absent` and point the user at the file. Measured: seven credential exposures across one corpus, one of them an account settings.json read whole as a session's first tool call. One row is WRITTEN rather than seeded (`written: true` - ALFRED_CODE_MEMORY_DB): it mirrors a choice the run just made (`--memory-level`) into the file the PLUGIN route's memory launcher reads, because a plugin MCP entry cannot expand a project env key (measured, spike S10 in docs/plugin-migration-evidence.md) while a launcher whose cwd is the project can read the file itself. A changed level has to land or the server keeps the old one, so a hand-edit is overwritten by the next install or update - change it with `--memory-level`, not by hand. A change to ANY of these takes effect on the NEXT TOOL CALL - every hook reads its value per invocation - so no session restart is ever needed. State that when reporting a flip: a run once told the user to restart, and `grep -rn restart` over stack/, meta/, scripts/ and setup-plugin/ found no such claim anywhere, so the model had invented it (the instrumentation ledger's first row in fact landed 27.2 s later in the same session, covering 63 of 65 calls). A fact about the stack's own behaviour that the stack does not state gets invented.

env.what: the generated-docs root every capture, loop and hook writes under. Default is machine-local (`.claude/*` is gitignored); a committed forward-slash path like `docs` shares the captured docs with the team. Existing docs never move with it.

how every capture's docs are VERSIONED - decided here, never guessed from git. `git`: the docs are committed and git versions them per branch, so a section is written into the doc file itself and nothing is ever written under `<docs-path>/.branches/` (promote and prune then have nothing to do). `local`: the machine-local overlay - a feature branch's sections live under `<docs-path>/.branches/<branch>/`, are merged into the mainline text at read time, and are folded into mainline when the branch merges. This decides HOW, never WHERE: the root stays ALFRED_CODE_DOCS_PATH. When the key is missing, the installers write `local` only if the docs are kept out of git - git ignores the docs root, or docs exist and none of them is committed - and `git` in every other case, a brand-new project included. `--docs-versioning git|local` (`-DocsVersioning` on Windows) writes a chosen value over the existing one; without it, an existing value is never touched. From then on the setting wins even where the repo disagrees, and `docs.js status` plus the session-start block report the disagreement rather than resolving it the other way.

the tool-usage instrumentation switch. `0` costs a node start per call that exits at the switch check and records nothing; `1` logs every tool call as one JSONL row for a measured run, then goes back to `0`. Flipping it takes effect on the next tool call; no session restart is needed.

the PUBLISH half of the commit gate: `git push` and `gh pr merge` need a `<docs-path>/flow/PUSH-GATE` receipt, the same shape the commit gate uses. Set `0` for a repo whose remote is already gated (branch protection, a required review). Measured: across four sessions every push and merge passed every guard - one published unpushed commits 18 minutes before any receipt existed, another put 40 files on a shared `develop`.

the stop contract's rotate ask once a credential shape has entered the session (a tool result, a paste). It asks ONCE per exposure: an answer covers every credential already in the transcript, and only a new one asks again. `0` turns it off for a user who accepts the exposure - the value is in the transcript either way.

the stop contract's done gate: a close claiming the change done, fixed, passing, works or ready is held once per turn when a source edit landed after the turn's last build or test run (or none ran), naming alfred-habits-done-gate. `0` turns it off.

guard-config-protection.js: an EXISTING lint / format / analyzer config (eslint, prettier, stylelint, biome, .editorconfig, a .ruleset) or a strictness setting in tsconfig / MSBuild (strict flags, NoWarn, TreatWarningsAsErrors, Nullable) cannot be changed to get a check green - weakening the check is the cheapest false pass. Creating a config passes; a change the user wants goes through one ask and the `<docs-path>/flow/CONFIG-EDIT-ALLOW` receipt. `0` turns the gate off.

monitor-session.js: a live monitor that never denies - the same tool with the same input 5 times in one turn, more than 20 distinct files written in one turn, the context at 80% of the fresh-session trigger. `log` writes one `mode: monitor` row per note to the hook-blocks ledger and injects nothing (the observation week); `inject` also hands the note back to the model; `0` is off.

check-turn-build.js: at Stop, ONE scoped build check per root for the source files the turn wrote - `tsc --noEmit -p` (the project's own tsc) for TypeScript, `dotnet build --no-restore -v q` for C# - the first 20 error lines handed back as a block, once per turn. `0` (the seed) is off; `1` turns it on, per project, after a measured week.

history-session.js: at Stop, a machine-local record of the session under `<docs-path>/history/` (its commits, the files left dirty, the user's AskUserQuestion answers - credential shapes scrubbed); at SessionStart, the last three records of the same branch injected in at most 600 chars. `1` (the seed) is on; `0` is off.

the per-message context, in TOKENS, at which a session on a 1M window is offered a fresh session instead of carrying on (an orchestration run is gated, a finished turn is offered). This row OWNS the whole gate: the two rows riding with it are the other window sizes, and `group_off` means the question also offers turning the feature off, which writes `0` to all three. The 400,000 default sits ABOVE the harness's own auto-compaction (measured preTokens 387,619-397,171), so on this window the turn-end offer is usually unreachable and the SessionStart compact route is what reaches you - lower it (250000, 350000) to be asked before the harness decides.

the same trigger in TOKENS for a 200k window. 150,000 is the measured figure - below it the offer nags, above it a 200k session has little room left to carry. `0` turns that tier off. The two tiers never interfere: each window size reads only its own variable.

the same trigger in TOKENS for every OTHER case - a window the gate cannot read (the model is not in `.claude/hooks/model-windows.json` and ALFRED_CODE_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW is unset) and a window that is neither of those two sizes. 180,000 is REACHABLE on the smallest window it could be applied to: at 250,000 it sat ABOVE a 200k window entirely, so a session on that tier could never trip the gate and it silently did not exist. An unproven window is assumed SMALL on purpose - an offer made a little early is one dismissible ask, while one that can never fire is no gate at all. `0` turns the offer off wherever the window is not one of the two named sizes.

the context WINDOW, in tokens, the fresh-session gate uses for a model `.claude/hooks/model-windows.json` does not list. That table (replaced on every update from the Claude models docs) is the ONLY other source - no id suffix, carry or compaction is read. Remove the key and an unlisted model takes ALFRED_CODE_FRESH_SESSION_DEFAULT.

the architecture docs hook's session-start block: ORIENTATION.md, this branch's doc overrides and conflicts, and how to read by section (also sent to dispatched subagents). `0` stops the push; promotion of merged branches still runs.
the first change under a source root waits until a covering doc section was read, and the hold hands that section over inline (at most two holds a session). `0` turns the hold off.
at session end, a change that hit the capture's watch.json asks once for the owning sections to be rewritten when a rule moved, or confirmed. `0` turns the ask off.

a csv of hook names this project switches off, e.g. `guard-answer-length,instrument-tool-usage`. It is where the guided walk's hooks LAYER lands: every hook now arrives together inside the core alfred-code plugin, so there is no file to leave out of an install, and the rows a setup or configure run does NOT pick are written here (that answer overwrites this value; every other run seeds it only when absent). Matching is exact on the base name, `.js` optional; a prefix never matches.

the shared `memory` MCP database this install points at - the path the `--memory-level` choice resolved to (`global` ~/.memory-mcp/memory.db, `scoped` ~/.memory-mcp/memory_<space>.db, `project` <project>/.memory-mcp/memory.db). The plugin route's launcher (`stack/mcp/memory-launch.js`) reads it from this file because a plugin MCP entry cannot expand a project env key; with the key absent it falls back to the global default. Written every run from the resolved level, never seeded - change it with `--memory-level` / `-MemoryLevel`, never by hand, and note that re-pointing the registration never moves or touches the old database file.
